# ubertooth

**Host tools for the Ubertooth One Bluetooth sniffer**

- **Version recorded:** 2020.12.R1
- **Categories:** `bluetooth`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/greatscottgadgets/ubertooth>

## What it does

The host-side utilities for the Ubertooth One: spectrum monitoring across 2.4 GHz, and capture of Bluetooth Low Energy traffic to a file other tools can read.

## Why you would want it

Bluetooth is one of the few common protocols an ordinary SDR handles badly -- it hops fast and wide -- and the Ubertooth is purpose-built for it. It is also one of the few pieces of RF-security hardware with a genuinely open design.

## Before it will work

Ubertooth One hardware, its udev rules and group membership from the hardware catalog, and firmware matching the host tools.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`rf-security`](../profiles/rf-security.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install ubertooth --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Commands it leaves on your PATH: `ubertooth-util-version`.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `ubertooth`

## Known problems

Host tools and device firmware are version-locked and a mismatch produces confusing failures rather than a clear error -- the single most common problem with this device. The three targets ship three different versions (Debian 13 2018.12.R1, Kali and Parrot 2020.12.R1), so the firmware you flash must match the tools your distribution gave you.

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade
